national.script: The weekend’s sports story: finishing strong. Cleveland won the deciding playoff game against Chicago, two to nothing, completing its series comeback. Oklahoma stunned top-ranked Texas, twenty-seven to twenty-four, with a field goal as time expired. Indiana rallied past Nebraska, twenty to seventeen. And Kentucky edged LSU, thirty-five to thirty-four, in overtime.
onscreen: Cleveland 2 — Chicago White Sox 0 | FINAL • OCT 10

localVariants.script: Down two games, still moving on. Cleveland beat Chicago two to nothing in the deciding playoff game, completing its series comeback. A two-run José Ramírez homer supplied the scoring.
The White Sox’s playoff run ended in Cleveland. Chicago fell two to nothing in the deciding game after leading the series two games to none. José Ramírez’s two-run homer made the difference.
Indiana found a way back. Trailing Nebraska seventeen to six in the fourth quarter, the Hoosiers rallied for a twenty-to-seventeen victory. An eleven-point deficit became a three-point win.

writtenCompanion: Saturday’s results offered three distinct finishes: a playoff-series reversal in Cleveland, a last-play rivalry upset in Dallas and a fourth-quarter rally by Indiana. Kentucky’s overtime victory added another close finish. Local editions select the most relevant lead while keeping results unchanged.
